error_events.evidence: db_agent reported at step 6 that H9ZU1C carries passengers 'James Moore, Ethan Lopez, and Amelia Sanchez'. The planner relayed only 'Ethan Johnson is not listed as a passenger or the user for reservation H9ZU1C. Therefore, he cannot be removed', dropping the passenger named Ethan (Lopez) that the customer's request ('remove Ethan') plainly refers to, and never asked policy_checker about passenger removal (the Modify-flight clause 'The user can modify passengers but cannot modify the number of passengers' is the actual reason).

Instructed db_agent 'Cancel the reservation with booking code H9ZU1C' without ever calling policy_checker (it is never called in this run) and without obtaining a cancellation reason. get_reservation_details at step 5 shows H9ZU1C is cabin 'economy', insurance 'no', created_at '2024-05-01T04:50:18' (current time 2024-05-15 15:00 EST), so under Cancel flight ('All reservations can be cancelled within 24 hours of booking, or if the airline cancelled the flight. Otherwise, basic economy or economy flights can be cancelled only if travel insurance is bought') this reservation was not cancellable. db_agent executed cancel_reservation at step 10, making the irreversible policy-violating change that the run is scored on (reward 0.0).

book_reservation called with invented arguments: user_id 'sara_doe_496' (the reservation it had just cancelled shows user_id 'mia_kim_4397'), passengers [{'first_name': 'John', 'last_name': 'Doe', 'age': 30}] and payment_methods ['gift_card_12345', 'gift_card_67890'] although get_user_details was never called anywhere in this run. Tool returned 'Error: user not found'. Only the user id was corrected (planner supplied mia_kim_4397 at step 28); the placeholder gift-card ids and the invented passenger record were carried into every later booking attempt (steps 29, 35, 46).

book_reservation flights entries use the key 'flight_id' ([{'flight_id': 'HAT069', ...}]) instead of the required 'flight_number' used in its own earlier call at step 24, so the tool returned "Error: 'flight_number'". The key was never corrected in any later attempt.

Misread the tool error: reported 'The booking failed due to an error related to the flight_number parameter. This might indicate an issue with the provided flight IDs (HAT069 and HAT276)'. The error "Error: 'flight_number'" is a missing key in its own arguments, not a bad flight number; the misdiagnosis sent the planner into a pointless availability re-check (steps 31-33 confirmed both flights available).

After step 33 confirmed HAT069 and HAT276 are available, it reissued a byte-identical book_reservation call still using 'flight_id' instead of 'flight_number' and got the same "Error: 'flight_number'" — a repeat of a known-failing call with no argument change.

'The cheapest option is EWR to LAX (HAT041) at $86 for Basic Economy' contradicts the list printed in the same message, which includes JFK to SEA (HAT069) at $51 basic economy (search_direct_flight result of step 40).

Report to the planner: 'The cheapest return option is LAX to EWR (HAT012) at $77 ... Combining this with the cheapest outbound flight (EWR to LAX, HAT041), the total cost for the round-trip in Basic Economy would be $163' — the same message lists SEA to JFK (HAT276) at $55 basic economy, so $77 is not the cheapest return, and $51 + $55 = $106 beats the $163 pairing offered to a customer who asked for the cheapest option.

Told the customer 'I found an alternative cheaper round-trip option ... EWR to LAX (HAT041) ... and LAX to EWR (HAT012) ..., with a total cost of $163 in Basic Economy'. $163 is more expensive than the $106 (JFK-SEA HAT069 $51 + SEA-JFK HAT276 $55) the planner itself quoted at step 21, so it is neither cheaper nor the cheapest the customer asked for.

Third book_reservation with the same malformed 'flight_id' keys (plus flight_type 'Round-trip', cabin 'Economy' although the quoted $163 are basic-economy fares, insurance 'No', and the still-invented payment_methods ['gift_card_12345','gift_card_67890']) -> "Error: 'flight_number'". No booking was ever made.

Repeats the same wrong diagnosis for the third time — 'This might indicate an issue with the provided flight IDs (HAT041 and HAT012) ... If the issue persists, contact a human agent' — although the error string names the missing 'flight_number' argument key and step 33 had already confirmed the flight numbers are valid and available.

Gave the customer invented contact details: 'Phone: 1-800-123-4567', 'Email: support@airline.com', 'Live Chat: Available on our website at www.airline.com/support'. None of this appears in any tool result, the customer's turns, or the policy, which states 'You should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools'; the environment's route to a human is the transfer_to_human_agents tool.
